bib.title: Attention-Based Recurrent Neural Network Models for Joint Intent Detection and Slot Filling

question: Can attention-based encoder-decoder and attention-based BiRNN models improve joint intent detection and slot filling on ATIS?
hypothesis: Attention on top of alignment-based RNNs, and joint training of intent and slots, should improve over independent models.
contributions: Strategies for using explicit alignment in attention encoder-decoder for slot filling
Attention-based BiRNN for joint intent detection and slot filling
State-of-the-art independent and joint results on ATIS

method.summary: Two joint models on a shared encoder: an LSTM encoder-decoder with aligned inputs and attention, and a BiRNN with attention context vector; intent decoded from attention-weighted hidden states. Evaluated on ATIS for slot F1 and intent error.
method.task: joint intent detection and slot filling (spoken language understanding)

datasets.name: ATIS (Hemphill et al. 1990; setup of Mesnil et al.)
datasets.size: 4978 train utterances (ATIS-2, ATIS-3); 893 test utterances (ATIS-3 NOV93, DEC94); 127 slot labels; 18 intents
datasets.source: shared by Gokhan Tur and Puyang Xu

datasets.name: Additional ATIS corpus (Xu & Sarikaya; Jeong & Lee)

models.name: Attention encoder-decoder (aligned inputs)
models.architecture: BiLSTM encoder, unidirectional LSTM decoder, additive attention, extra intent decoder sharing encoder

models.name: Attention BiRNN
models.architecture: BiLSTM; hidden state combined with attention context vector for slots; intent from attention-weighted (or mean-pooled + logistic regression without attention) hidden states

training.objective: max likelihood of slot labels (Eq 1); intent and slot costs back-propagated jointly to shared encoder
training.optimizer: Adam, suggested parameter setup of Kingma & Ba
training.regularisation: gradient clipping max norm 5; forget gate bias 1

inference.samples: Table 1 reports best and average +- std over unstated number of runs; Tables 2-5 single numbers

eval.protocol: Single test set for ATIS; 10-fold CV for additional corpus. Number of runs and seeds not stated; no significance test.

results.claim: Joint training of attention BiRNN improves intent error by 0.56 absolute over independent training.
results.setup: ATIS, 4978 train / 893 test utterances, 127 slot labels, 18 intents, 1-layer LSTM 128 units; joint vs independent BiRNN; 23.8% relative
results.quote: 0.56% absolute gain (23.8% relative improvement) on intent detection over the independent training models

results.claim: Joint attention BiRNN gains 0.23 slot F1 over independent training.
results.setup: ATIS, 4978 train / 893 test utterances, 127 slot labels, 18 intents, 1-layer LSTM 128 units

results.claim: Joint encoder-decoder gains 0.45 absolute (22.2% relative) on intent error and 0.09 F1.
results.setup: ATIS, 4978 train / 893 test utterances, 127 slot labels, 18 intents, 1-layer LSTM 128 units
results.quote: 0.45% absolute gain (22.2% relative improvement) on intent detection

results.claim: Joint attention BiRNN reaches 95.98 F1 and 1.79% intent error, best of joint models.
results.setup: ATIS, 4978 train / 893 test utterances, 127 slot labels, 18 intents, 1-layer LSTM 128 units; Table 4; best-run numbers
results.table: Table 4, row Attention BiRNN, column F1 Score (1.79 intent error)

results.claim: Joint attention encoder-decoder gets 95.87 F1, 1.57% intent error.
results.setup: ATIS, 4978 train / 893 test utterances, 127 slot labels, 18 intents, 1-layer LSTM 128 units
results.table: Table 4, row Attention Encoder-Decoder NN, column Intent Error (%)

results.claim: Independent attention encoder-decoder intent error 2.02%, BiRNN 2.35%, vs boosting+simplified sentences 3.02%.
results.setup: ATIS, 4978 train / 893 test utterances, 127 slot labels, 18 intents, 1-layer LSTM 128 units
results.table: Table 3, row Attention Encoder-Decoder NN, column Error (%)

results.claim: Independent attention BiRNN slot F1 95.75 best; average 95.42 +- 0.18.
results.setup: ATIS, 4978 train / 893 test utterances, 127 slot labels, 18 intents, 1-layer LSTM 128 units
results.table: Table 1, row BiRNN with attention, column F1 Score
results.note: Average 95.42 +- 0.18; attention adds ~0.05 average over no attention (95.37), within the std

results.claim: Encoder-decoder without aligned inputs performs poorly on slot filling.
results.setup: ATIS, 4978 train / 893 test utterances, 127 slot labels, 18 intents, 1-layer LSTM 128 units

results.claim: On the additional ATIS corpus (10-fold CV) attention BiRNN gets 95.78 F1 and 5.60% intent error.
results.setup: additional ATIS corpus 5138 utterances, 110 slots, 21 intents, 10-fold CV
results.table: Table 5, row Attention BiRNN, column F1 Score (5.60 intent error)

limits: Only ATIS and one additional ATIS corpus; average sentence length 11, authors say the BiRNN hidden state already encodes most needed information so attention adds little for slots
Joint results in Tables 4-5 are single numbers with no variance; no significance test
One LSTM layer only; deeper models left to future work
Learning rate, epochs, hardware and seeds not stated
Attention weights are mostly evenly distributed; only a few insightful cases
